problem: Embodied navigation agents (PointNav/ObjectNav) are evaluated only on unseen scenes that share the training scenes' appearance and dynamics. No benchmark measured how trained agents behave when the egocentric RGB sensor is degraded (blur, noise, spatter, cracked lens, low light, narrower FOV) or when actuation is corrupted (friction-like bias, drift, motor failure).
motivation: Deployed robots face sensor degradation and actuation changes such as different floor friction, dirty lenses and failing motors. Calibrating for every target environment does not scale, so agents should resist or adapt to these shifts with little unsupervised interaction. Simulation lets researchers study a wide, reproducible set of such corruptions quickly, safely and cheaply before real-robot deployment.
key_idea: RobustNav builds a RoboTHOR-based benchmark in which agents trained in clean scenes are tested in unseen validation scenes under 7 visual and 4 dynamics corruptions (plus combinations), with an optional ~166k-step unsupervised calibration budget. It is used to measure degradation, diagnose failure behaviors, and test whether data augmentation or self-supervised adaptation (PAD) recovers performance.
insight: Corruption difficulty for static vision does not transfer to embodied tasks. Defocus Blur and Speckle Noise are the worst corruptions for ImageNet ResNet-18 (9.39 / 7.79 top-1), yet Spatter (33.58 SR) and Lower-FOV (42.49 SR) are far worse for PointNav-RGB, so robustness must be measured in-task. A clean depth channel largely immunizes PointNav against RGB corruptions: RGB-D leads RGB by 36.09-60.09 absolute SPL under Spatter, Lower-FOV and Speckle Noise. ObjectNav failures are driven largely by a broken stopping mechanism: an oracle stop adds +7.12 SR when clean and +13.88 under Defocus Blur + Motion Drift. Data augmentation mainly helps Lower-FOV (+22.81 SPL) and hurts Spatter. PAD with Action-Prediction adaptation consistently degrades performance; Rotation-Prediction adaptation improves over its pretrained version but stays at least 20.39 SPL below clean. Supervised finetuning within the same budget almost fully recovers performance except for Lower-FOV, so the gap lies in the unsupervised adaptation method, not the budget.
method: Visual corruptions (7): Spatter, Motion Blur, Defocus Blur and Speckle Noise (from ImageNet-C) and Low Lighting, each at severities 1-5; Lower-FOV (79° to 39.5°); Camera Crack (randomized crack with fixed seeds per val scene). Main results use severity 5.

Dynamics corruptions (4 + PyRobot): Motion Bias (C), a constant per-episode bias of ±0.05/0.1/0.15 m or ±5/10/15°; Motion Bias (S), per-step N(0.25 m, 0.1 m) translation and N(30°, 10°) rotation; Motion Drift, forward moves drifting α=10° (≤~0.043 m lateral); Motor Failure, where rotate-left or rotate-right fails for the whole episode. The PyRobot ILQR LoCoBot noise model is also included. All run on top of LoCoBot-calibrated actuation noise except Motion Bias (S).

Protocol: train on the 60 clean RoboTHOR train scenes; evaluate on the 15 corrupted val scenes (1100 PointNav / 1095 ObjectNav episodes, split into easy/medium/hard by shortest path). A ~166k-step unsupervised calibration budget is allowed in the target. Future work should not train on the reserved target corruptions.

Agents: frozen ImageNet ResNet-18 encoder, then a 1x1-conv compressor (512→128→32 ×7×7). The goal encoder is a linear 2→32 layer on polar coordinates for PointNav or a 12×32 object embedding for ObjectNav. A 1x1-conv combiner feeds a 1-layer GRU (512) with actor-critic heads, in RGB and RGB-D variants.

Training: DD-PPO + GAE in AllenAct. Reward is 10·success − Δgeodesic − 0.01 per step. PointNav trains ~75M frames and ObjectNav ~300M frames under LoCoBot actuation noise N(0.25 m, 0.005 m) / N(30°, 0.5°).

Behavior diagnostics: failed actions (collisions), minimum and terminal distance to target, Stop-Fail (Pos) (end called out of range) and Stop-Fail (Neg) (no end while in range), and SR with an oracle stopping mechanism.

Robustness baselines: data augmentation (Random-Crop, Random-Shift, Color-Jitter); PAD with Action-Prediction or Rotation-Prediction auxiliary heads, pretrained then self-supervised adapted in the corrupted target for ~166k steps; supervised finetuning in the target as an upper bound.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-pretrained, frozen) + GRU actor-critic policy trained from scratch with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: RoboTHOR 60 training scenes (clean, with LoCoBot actuation noise). PointNav agents trained ~75M frames, ObjectNav agents ~300M frames. Variants: data-augmented training; PAD auxiliary pretraining plus ~166k steps of unsupervised adaptation in the target.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB or RGB-D (224×224); PointNav additionally has GPS+Compass
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE_AHEAD 0.25 m, ROTATE_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, END (ObjectNav adds LOOK_UP/LOOK_DOWN 30°); max 300 steps
setting.simulator: RoboTHOR (AI2-THOR); Habitat/Gibson only for an OccAnt checkpoint evaluation
setting.privileged: none (PointNav uses the standard GPS+Compass sensor)

numbers_note: Main numbers come from Table 2 (single evaluation, severity 5). Appendix Table 5 repeats them as mean±stderr over 3 seeds and adds severity 3 and PyRobot combinations (e.g. Clean PointNav RGB 98.97±0.18 SR / 83.45±0.27 SPL; Clean ObjectNav RGB 31.78±0.81 / 14.50±0.47). Tables 6-7 break results down by easy/medium/hard episodes. Table 3 also reports AP-based PAD rows and a supervised-finetune upper bound (e.g. Spatter 91.81 SR / 77.38 SPL), not all listed here. Table 4 evaluates a third-party OccAnt checkpoint on Gibson val (not the authors' method; omitted). Behavior metrics (collisions, distances, Stop-Fail, oracle-stop SR gains) are given only in Figures 4, 7 and 8.
results: Standard DD-PPO agents degrade sharply under corruptions. PointNav-RGB drops from 98.82 SR / 83.13 SPL (clean) to 33.58/24.72 under Spatter, 42.49/31.73 under Lower-FOV and 20.56/17.63 under Motor Failure. ObjectNav-RGB drops from 31.05/14.26 to 5.02/2.42 under Defocus Blur, and combined visual+dynamics corruptions hurt further. RGB-D PointNav is nearly unaffected by visual corruptions (e.g. 98.91 SR under Spatter) but not by Motor Failure (20.56). Data augmentation best recovers Lower-FOV (71.70 SR / 54.54 SPL) and PAD rotation-prediction adaptation best recovers Spatter (61.06 / 47.16). Neither closes the gap to clean performance, whereas supervised finetuning within the 166k-step budget nearly does.
limitations: Corruptions are synthetic approximations of real sensor and actuation faults. Friction is only emulated via motion bias because RoboTHOR lacks multiple friction zones.
Only simple end-to-end RL agents in RoboTHOR are benchmarked (plus one OccAnt check on Gibson); there is no real-robot validation.
Robustness and adaptation baselines (data augmentation, PAD) are studied only for visual corruptions and only for PointNav-RGB; no dynamics-adaptation methods are evaluated.
